simple.meaning: שַׁפְרוּר (shaphrûwr) is a Hebrew action word meaning “splendid , i.e. a tapestry or canopy.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Jeremiah, beginning at Jeremiah 43:10. The surrounding contexts include kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שַׁפְרוּר (H8237) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שַׁפְרוּר (shaphrûwr) / H8237 is traced through Jeremiah 43:10 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: splendid , i.e. a tapestry or canopy
definitions.full: H8237. shaphrur or shaphrir [ שׁפרור Kt, שַׁפְרִיר Qr] noun [masculine] doubtful, Thes splendour (√ שׁפר ; Dl Prol. 126 compare Assyrian verb šuparruru , spread out (Id HAW 684 )); apparently of ( brightly-coloured ? ) royal pavilion, canopy , or possibly carpet , suffix שׁפרורו נָטָה Jer 43:10 (Qr שַׁפָרִירוֺ ). [ שָׁפַת ], מִשְׁמְּתַיִם אַעשׁמֹּת, see II. שׁפה .

occurrences.englishText: and tell them, Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: ‘Behold, I will send and take Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and will set his throne on these stones that I have hidden; and he will spread his royal pavilion over them.
